evidence.mechanism: shot-08s: six oxblood arms with dense fern-like side branches grow out from a central hub on rose-clay; by shot-20s the branching has filled out into feathered arms, so the growth visibly develops.
evidence.ambition: shot-08s: one flat 2D layer with a soft radial vignette and no material or lighting; the only extra idea is the mirrored glyph row seen at shot-02s, so ambition stays modest.
evidence.craft: shot-02s: mirrored glyph fragments 'ectd' and 'pect' sit along the arms and specks cluster at the tips, while the figure is pushed to the upper-left; shot-20s is cleaner, with a coherent rose and oxblood palette.
evidence.distinctness: shot-20s: oxblood six-arm fern on a rose-clay ground, unlike the ochre and rust Penrose kite tiling on cream from 2026-11-23; the six-armed snowflake form itself is a common cliche.
evidence.polish: shot-02s: figure sits off-centre with arms clipped at the top and left edges and the right half empty; by shot-20s the figure is centred and resolved, clearly differing from the opening frame.

pairwise_justification: shot-20s: one centred six-arm fern on rose-clay reads as a single clear figure at thumbnail size, while the median's 20s is a dense ochre and rust tile field on cream with less shape contrast.

critique.change: Keep the fixed-lag rule visible after 2 s: the glyph row 'defect' vanishes by shot-08s, so make each letter birth a visible side arm at a constant distance behind the tip in shot-08s and shot-20s.
Centre the six-arm figure at shot-02s and stop the arms clipping at the top and left edges, so the opening frame is composed rather than pushed into one corner.
Replace the flat oxblood fill on the arms with a ridge highlight or simple shading, so shot-08s and shot-20s gain material and a second rendering idea beyond one flat layer.
